resources.string: RetroForge follows your phone\'s language when it has it. Choose another here. Some screens are still in English while the translations are finished.
HD textures that make N64 and PSP games look sharper than the original. Download free N64 packs, or add your own.
Look for new games when RetroForge starts

Each time RetroForge opens, it checks the game folders on this phone, so games you add show up by themselves. Network drives aren\'t checked (too slow over Wi-Fi): rescan those in Retro → Game folders.
Show systems you have no games for
On: the Retro tab lists every system RetroForge supports. Off: only the systems you have games for.
Turn off to hide the PC tab, if you only play retro games or this device can\'t run PC games.
Shows which graphics chip this device has. On Snapdragon phones, it also downloads Turnip drivers, which can make emulator apps like Dolphin, Eden and NetherSX2 run better.
While you hold R2, the game runs fast, to skip slow text and cutscenes. Only on systems whose controllers had no R2 (Game Boy, GBA, NES, SNES, Mega Drive …).
Small sounds as you move around with a controller or remote, and when you select something or go back.
Open your other apps and Android\'s settings from RetroForge, or make RetroForge the home screen (good for handhelds and TV boxes).
A short guide to every feature: playing, emulators, hotkeys, covers, playlists, the ROM Manager and more.
With a controller: D-pad to move, A to select, B to go back, L1/R1 to switch tabs.
Who made it, what it does, and where the name comes from.
Checks every system you have games for: is its emulator ready, are its BIOS files in place, were games found? Problems are listed first.
Step by step: pick your games folder, get the emulators your systems need (downloaded for you) and add your BIOS files.

Thousands of fan-made covers to choose from. To use them, make a free SteamGridDB account, tap \"Get a free key\", then copy the key and paste it here. It stays on this device and is only sent to SteamGridDB.
Use \"Change cover\" on any game to browse SteamGridDB covers.

As well as the built-in player, games can open in RetroArch or in free emulator apps you install yourself (pick one on a game\'s page). Obtainium installs them from their official releases and keeps them up to date.
To add a whole set at once: get the Obtainium Emulation Pack file, then in Obtainium open Import/Export → Obtainium Import and pick the file.

Button combos that work in games RetroForge opens in RetroArch. Your RetroArch settings aren\'t changed: RetroForge adds a small file in Documents/RetroForge with these buttons. Other emulator apps use their own menus and buttons.
ScreenScraper needs RetroForge\'s own developer ID, which ScreenScraper issues on request. It will work once that\'s added.
Optional: sign in with a free ScreenScraper account to download more covers each day. Your login stays on this device and is only sent to ScreenScraper. Use \"Change cover\" on a game to look it up.

For two-screen devices like the AYN Thor and AYANEO Pocket DS. On: a DS game\'s top screen fills the main display and its touch screen goes to the second one. Off: both DS screens on the main display. Select to switch.

Play a game with a friend on another device: open a game and choose Play together, or use Netplay in the game\'s menu. Same Wi-Fi, or over the internet (RetroForge asks your router to let your friend in).
Buttons work this many frames late on both devices, so they arrive in time. 2 or 3 on the same Wi-Fi; 4 to 6 over the internet. The host\'s setting is used.
Play this game with a friend on another device, each with RetroForge and the same game file. One hosts (player 1), the other joins (player 2).
Looking for games on this Wi-Fi…
Nobody\'s hosting on this Wi-Fi yet.
From libretro\'s cheat database (CC BY-SA 4.0). Switch one on and it works at once. Cheats can upset saves: save your game first.
Works in a level (picked elsewhere, it waits for the next one). Can\'t be turned off until the game is restarted.
Select a setting to change it. Kept for this emulator.
Select a button, then press the controller button you want for it. Kept for this system.
Select one to change which game button it presses.
The game restarts in the emulator you pick and your in-game save carries over. Save states belong to each emulator.
You can read this again any time in Settings.
Nothing sharing files found on this Wi-Fi. Check the PC is on, on the same network, and has a shared folder.
PC or NAS name or address (e.g. 192.168.1.20)
Pick a shared folder above, then add it. For a folder inside a share, type it after a slash (Retrobat/roms).
The password stays on this device and is only sent to that PC or NAS.
Long-press an app to pin it here (or unpin it).
Use RetroForge as the home screen

For handhelds and TV boxes: the device starts in RetroForge and the home button comes back here. Select to switch, then choose the home app in Android\'s list. To undo, select again and pick your old home app.
Add your game folder in Retro and the hacks you already have (folders such as \"SMW HACKS\") will appear here.
No hacks found in your folders. Folders with \"hack\" in their name, and files tagged (Hack) or [h], are listed here.
No hacks yet. Add a catalogue below.
Needs these patches first, in this order
Choose a catalogue .json file on this device.
Paste the https:// address of a catalogue .json file. RetroForge downloads only that file, and only when you confirm.
ROM hacks you already have, and more to discover from your catalogues.
Catalogues list hacks and link to their pages. They never contain ROMs or patches. Format: docs/hack-catalogue-format.md
Add your games folder in Retro to fill the bar.
Play a game and it appears here, big.
Play a game and it shows up here.
Favourite a game from its page.
Make playlists from any game\'s page.
Merging the past, building the future
Add your games folder in Retro (or run Settings → Set up RetroForge), and your collection shows up here.
Ports of your games, and Windows games on supported devices.
Your other apps and Android\'s settings. Also where RetroForge can become the home screen.
From libretro\'s free thumbnail library, matched to your file name.
SteamGridDB has thousands of community-made covers. Add your own free API key in Settings to browse them here.
SteamGridDB didn\'t accept your API key. Check it in Settings.
No games found. Try a shorter or different name.
No covers for this game yet.
Covers are made by SteamGridDB\'s community; the artist is credited under each one.
Not available in this build: ScreenScraper needs RetroForge\'s own developer ID, which ScreenScraper issues on request.
Front and 3D boxes from ScreenScraper\'s database, matched by your file. Add your ScreenScraper account in Settings for a higher daily limit.
ScreenScraper has no box art for this file.
Use any picture saved on this device, for example a cover scan from The Cover Project (thecoverproject.net), which RetroForge can\'t download from directly.
Removes the chosen cover. The game shows its gamelist artwork again, if it has any.
Changes are saved in RetroForge only. The game file and any gamelist.xml stay as they are, and rescans keep your changes.

Select to choose the folder that holds your system folders, such as an existing \"roms\" folder from another frontend (with snes, nes, psx … inside), or a single system folder. RetroForge only reads it: nothing is renamed, moved or written unless you use the ROM Manager and allow it.
Select to add folders, rescan or see problems.
Apply IPS, BPS or UPS patches (ROM hacks, translations) to make a new copy. Originals are never changed.
Tidy duplicate copies and compress games (CHD for discs, .zip for cartridges). Shows every change first and can undo it; files are set aside, not deleted.
Android no longer lets RetroForge read this folder (the drive may have been removed, or access was withdrawn). Forget it and add it again.
No system folders were found here. Choose the folder that contains snes, nes, psx …, or a single system folder.
A \"roms\" folder from another frontend, a single system folder, or a folder on an SD card or USB drive. \"Forget folder\" removes only RetroForge\'s index.
No gamelist.xml details for this game; the title comes from its file name.
Same game and tags, different file. RetroForge doesn\'t delete anything; this is for your information.

Two players, two devices, the same game. To host: open a game and choose Play together → Host. To join a friend on this Wi-Fi, find their game below; over the internet, open the game and choose Play together → Join.
Nobody\'s hosting on this Wi-Fi right now.
Pick one to open your copy, then choose Play together → Join.
Your consoles, arcade and computer games.
RetroForge keeps its own index of these folders. Your files are only read, unless you allow the ROM Manager to change them.
This core needs BIOS files in RetroArch\'s system folder.
Use the built-in player by default
Saturn in the built-in player is experimental: some games stay on a black screen. RetroArch or Yaba Sanshiro 2 (below) play more of them.
Two players on two devices, each with RetroForge and this game: one hosts, the other joins. Same Wi-Fi or over the internet.
This game is made of several files. Most standalone emulators can only open it if you also add your game folder inside the emulator.
Tip: Obtainium installs emulators from their official releases and keeps them updated.
Make playlist and add this game
Empty so far. Open a game and use \"Add to a playlist\".
Only the playlist goes. The games stay in your library and on your storage.
Retro games, handhelds and PC gaming
Channels and sites worth following. Links open in YouTube or your browser.
Add a game folder in Retro first.
Keep RetroForge open until this finishes. Stopping is safe: the game in progress is left as it was.
Each game moves into the folder for its system (made if needed). Favourites, playlists and play history go with them. Other frontends will find them there too. Undo from History puts every file back.

Each multi-disc game gets an .m3u playlist next to its discs, listing them in order. Your disc files aren\'t changed. RetroForge then shows each game once, and the emulator can change discs from its menu. Other frontends will list the playlist too.
If another frontend uses this folder on a PC, close it first: some rewrite gamelist.xml when they exit.
Looks for the same game in several files (e.g. a .zip and a .7z) and checks whether they hold the same data. This only reads your files.

Disc games (.cue/.bin, and PS2/PSP .iso) become CHD, which RetroArch, DuckStation, Flycast, NetherSX2 and PPSSPP play directly. Cartridge ROMs become .zip. This only reads your files until you confirm.
Everything that can be compressed already is.
A CHD is usually 30–60% smaller; audio CD tracks shrink less.
Sort loose games into system folders

Finds games outside a folder for their system (loose files, a Downloads or Extras folder) and shows where each would go: the folder you already use for that system, or a new one named like RetroBat and ES-DE. This only reads your files.
Every game is already in its system\'s folder.
Finds games split over several discs or floppies (\"Disc 1\", \"Disk 2 of 4\", \"Side B\") that have no .m3u playlist, so each plays as one game with disc swapping. This only reads your files.
Every multi-disc game already has a playlist.
Files RetroForge set aside. Delete a folder once you\'re sure you don\'t need it: this is the only step that deletes for good.
Can\'t be undone: its files were deleted permanently
Tidy duplicates and compress games. Every change is shown first and History can undo it. Files are set aside, never deleted, until you choose Free up space.

\"Use RetroForge\'s film folders\" makes Movies/RetroForge on your phone, with a Films folder and a 3D Films folder inside. Choose \"Use this folder\" when Android asks, then copy films into them (USB cable or a file manager) and press Look again. Or choose any folder you already keep films in, on the phone, an SD card or a USB drive. RetroForge only reads it.
3D films (side by side or top and bottom) get a 3D badge and play in Cardboard modes. How to watch: Settings → How to use RetroForge → Media.
No films found in that folder (mp4, mkv, avi, mov and others).
No 3D films yet. Films with 3D, SBS, HSBS, TAB or HOU in their name (or in a \"3D Films\" folder) show here.
No 3D films yet. Put them in Movies/RetroForge/3D Films (Media → Use RetroForge\'s film folders) or name them with 3D, SBS or TAB, and they show here.

RetroForge uses the poster and .nfo file saved next to each film, as Kodi, Plex and Jellyfin do (Film-poster.jpg or Film.jpg, poster.jpg in a film\'s own folder, Film.nfo or movie.nfo). Media Companion or tinyMediaManager on a PC make them for a whole collection. Films without them show a frame from the film.

Optional, for your own use: a free TMDB key (create an account at themoviedb.org, copy your API key v3, paste it here) fills in films that have no poster of their own. It stays on this device and is sent only to TMDB. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
Your films, with artwork, played right here.

Watch films from Plex, Jellyfin, Emby or a NAS on your home network, with no sign-in: RetroForge finds them the way smart TVs and Bigscreen do (DLNA). In Plex: Settings → DLNA → Enable the DLNA server (on by default).
Select to choose a ROM (.zip and .7z are fine).
Matches once the 512-byte header is removed
Checked against the result of the patches above when applied.
No readme found. Check the patch\'s download page for the ROM version and patch order it needs.
Apply IPS, BPS or UPS patches. Your original ROM is never changed; the result is saved as a new file you choose.

GeForce NOW and Boosteroid stream PC games you own on Steam, Epic and other stores; Amazon Luna plays in your browser. Each is a separate service with its own sign-in and plans, in its official app or site.

Games their makers let anyone share: shareware episodes (Doom, Wolfenstein 3D, Commander Keen), freeware and new homebrew for old consoles. They come from RetroArch\'s own download server and play in RetroForge\'s built-in player. Abandonware isn\'t offered: those games are still owned by someone.
First, choose where they go: your roms folder (the one with snes, psx … inside) is best.

Install games in GameNative (Steam, Epic, GOG, Amazon) or export their shortcuts from Winlator Cmod or WinNative. Shortcut files (.steam, .epic, .gog, .amazon, .pcgame, .desktop) in a \"windows\" or \"steam\" folder beside snes, psx and the rest are found by themselves. Or add a Windows game\'s folder to play it in RetroForge\'s own PC player (early test: the first game downloads the PC runtime, about 280 MB).
There\'s no .exe in the game\'s folder.

GameNative (Steam, Epic, GOG and Amazon games you own) and Winlator (Windows games you have installed) are free, separately developed apps. Their recent versions and community builds are reported to run some games on Mali and Xclipse GPUs too, usually with lower compatibility than on Snapdragon. RetroForge doesn\'t start their games yet and hasn\'t tested them.
Based on DroidDeck\'s published requirements; a supported GPU does not guarantee every game runs.
DroidDeck, the PC runtime RetroForge works with, needs a Qualcomm Snapdragon chip (Adreno GPU). Your retro games work as normal.
Select this card to open it.
Your PC games, cloud gaming, ports and free games.
Your PC\'s games on this screen

Play games running on your own Windows, Linux or Mac computer here, with your controller or touch. The PC needs Sunshine, a free streaming host (or an NVIDIA graphics card with GeForce Experience\'s GameStream), on the same network. RetroForge streams with Moonlight\'s open-source code built in, so there\'s no other app to install here.
No PCs answered. Type its address below instead (on the PC: Settings > Network shows its IP address).
Every PC that answered is already in your list.
It didn\'t answer. Check the PC is on, awake and running Sunshine.
The PC lists no apps. Add some in Sunshine\'s Applications page.
Choose one to stream full screen. Press back (or Start+Select+L1+R1 on a controller) to stop streaming; the game keeps running on the PC until you quit it.
None of your games has a port in this list yet.
How: download the Windows version from its releases page and unzip it into Download/RetroForge/Ports. Then in GameNative (or Winlator) add it as a custom game and pick its .exe.

Steam games check that Steam is running and that you own them. Sign in so RetroForge can get each game\'s ticket from Steam, as GameNative does. Your password goes to Steam only; RetroForge keeps just the sign-in token Steam gives it.

Stream Xbox games from xbox.com/play, improved by Better xCloud. Most games need Game Pass Premium or Ultimate; some free-to-play games such as Fortnite don\'t. You sign in on Microsoft\'s own page. Not made or endorsed by Microsoft.
Built with AI: the code, the built-in player and the guides were written with Claude, Anthropic\'s AI, working to Darren\'s ideas, tested on real phones and checked by him. No secret about it.
…sorry, wrong YouTube channel. (A nod to Mr Sujano. Go and subscribe to him.)
RetroForge doesn\'t stand for anything. It\'s what it does: it forges all of retro gaming into one place, so you set it up once and then just play.
• Finds the games you already have, on your phone or SD card, and shows them with box art, by system, or on a bookshelf.

• Plays them in its own built-in player, with nothing to set up, or in RetroArch and standalone emulators. Bezels, filters, cheats, save states, and netplay with friends on the same Wi-Fi or over the internet.
• Plays Windows PC games itself, in its own PC player: your Steam library with artwork, downloads and Steam Cloud saves, an on-screen Xbox controller (or your own), and Play together for LAN games.
• Streams the games on your own PC (Moonlight and Sunshine), and opens cloud gaming like Xbox Cloud Gaming.
• On Snapdragon devices, can use the open-source Turnip driver in its own players for faster GPU games.
• Keeps your saves in step between devices, and has free games to download and play.
• Patches ROM hacks and translations, and helps you discover more from catalogues you choose.
• Tidies your collection: removes duplicates, compresses discs to CHD and cartridges to .zip, and makes multi-disc playlists. Every change is shown first and can be undone.
• Works with a controller from the sofa as well as with touch.

Retro gaming on Android usually means a frontend, an emulator per system, a scraper, a patcher, a file manager and a pile of forum threads. RetroForge\'s aim is to bring all of that together: easy first setup, sensible defaults, and the power tools there when you want them.
It works alongside what you already have. Your folders stay where they are, other frontends keep working, and nothing changes on disk unless you confirm it.
Bezels in the built-in player are by The Bezel Project (github.com/thebezelproject), downloaded from their GitHub when you ask.

The PC player stands on Wine, Proton, FEX, DXVK and Mesa, with the builds GameNative and Winlator Cmod made for Android. Turnip drivers are built by K11MCH1 and MrPurple from Mesa\'s code, and loaded with libadrenotools by Billy Laws.
RetroForge comes with no games and no BIOS files. Use your own copies of games and BIOS you own.

Artwork round the game in landscape, like RetroArch and RetroBat bezels: a frame for each system, and for most games their own. Made by The Bezel Project (github.com/thebezelproject) and downloaded from their GitHub, not included in RetroForge. Download a system below; each game\'s own bezel (about 150 KB) is fetched the first time it starts. Bezels match No-Intro file names. Select this card to switch them on or off; Picture in the game\'s menu switches a system.
None of the systems in your library have Bezel Project bezels.

RetroForge has its own emulators for most systems, from Game Boy to PS2 and GameCube, downloaded in the background. In a game, swipe in from the left or right edge for the menu: save states, screen shape, filters, buttons, cheats, widescreen, Cardboard VR and switching emulator.
Carry on where you left off
When you quit a game, your place is saved, and the game starts from there next time. In the built-in player and in RetroArch.
The emulator each system uses (tap to change):

Resolution makes 3D games sharper than the console did: 2× looks like 720p, 3× like 1080p, up to 10× for PSP, but higher needs a faster phone. Graphics: GameCube, Wii and PS2 use Vulkan; other systems use OpenGL, with Vulkan (experimental) as an option that can be faster (switch back if a game goes black). Both can be changed in a game\'s menu too.
Disc games: play straight away or copy first

Big disc games (PlayStation, Dreamcast, Saturn …) and arcade games start straight away from your folder or network drive, without copying. If they stutter on slow Wi-Fi, choose Copy first: the game is copied to the phone before it starts, and the last two are kept so they start faster next time. Some emulators always copy.

Puts your game saves, save states, cheats, settings, favourites and playlists into one zip file. Keep it somewhere safe, or restore it on a new phone (add your game folders first, so favourites and playlists find their games). Restoring replaces files with the same name and keeps the rest.
Turns your ES-DE custom collections into RetroForge playlists, with the games found in your library. Pick ES-DE\'s folder (or its collections folder); ES-DE\'s files aren\'t changed.
Try one driver at a time. If a game gets worse, switch that emulator back to the system driver.

The built-in player\'s Vulkan cores (Dolphin, PS2, PSP on Vulkan) and the PC player can use a Turnip driver instead of the phone\'s own: often faster, and it lets older Adrenos run the PC player\'s fast Direct3D (DXVK).
What graphics chip this device has, and custom drivers for emulators that can use them.
RetroForge\'s hotkeys are off, so RetroArch uses its own settings.

DuckStation, Dolphin, PPSSPP and the other standalone apps have their own menus and hotkeys, set in each app\'s settings. RetroForge can\'t change them, because Android doesn\'t let one app read the controller while another is on screen.
Change the RetroArch combos under Settings → RetroArch hotkeys.
RetroForge is built with these open-source parts. Select one to read its licence text where it ships with the app.

RetroArch, standalone emulators, DroidDeck and Obtainium are separate apps with their own licences; RetroForge only opens them. No games, BIOS or firmware are included. Covers come from libretro, SteamGridDB or ScreenScraper when you ask, under their own terms.
RetroForge stands on the work of a lot of people. Thank you all.

Each PlayStation game in the built-in player has its own memory card. Pick one to see its saves, then copy a save to another game\'s card (handy for sequels that read the first game\'s save) or delete it. You can also open a card file from another emulator (.mcr, .mcd, .mc, .gme) and copy its saves across. Quit the game first: a game that\'s running writes its own card back. A game gets its card the first time it\'s played.
Save this card as a file (.mcr)
Your library, play history, favourites, playlists, covers, settings, themes, ROM Manager history and any keys or logins you add stay in RetroForge\'s private storage. Uninstalling deletes them.
• libretro thumbnails, for box art: system and game names.
• SteamGridDB, when you search covers: your search and your own API key.
• ScreenScraper, when you look a game up: its file name, size and checksum, RetroForge\'s developer ID and your login if you added one.
• Hack catalogues you added, when you refresh them.
Links you open (emulator pages, hack pages, videos) go to your browser.
RetroForge reads the folders you choose and changes files only when you confirm a ROM Manager action. Nothing is uploaded.
RetroForge collects nothing about you: no accounts, no analytics, no ads, no tracking.

Keeps your in-game saves (and save states) the same on all your devices. Choose a folder that every device can reach: one on a network drive (your PC), or a folder on this device that a cloud app keeps in step (Syncthing, FolderSync, Autosync for Google Drive, Nextcloud, OneDrive …). A game\'s saves come in when it starts and go back when you quit. If a save changed on two devices, the newer one is kept and the other is put in the \"sync conflicts\" folder. Nothing is ever deleted. Built-in player only.
To sync through your PC, add it first under Games and library → Game folders → Network drives.
Every system you have games for: its emulator, its BIOS and its games.
RetroForge is free, with every feature included, and always will be. If you\'re enjoying it, a coffee helps pay for new features and bug fixes. Thank you!
Scan with your phone, or use the button below.

Free HD packs by GhostlyDark, downloaded from their official GitHub releases. Downloads are 150 MB to over 1 GB, so use Wi-Fi, and unpacked they take several times that space (Smash Bros. is about 1.2 GB). Made for the USA versions of the games. They\'re switched on automatically.
High-resolution textures for games in the built-in player.
Some themes are dark-only or light-only and keep their look either way.
A RetroForge theme is one small .json file (format in docs/retroforge-theme-format.md). Themes are only data: nothing in them runs.

From another frontend: choose a theme folder from another frontend (EmulationStation-style themes). RetroForge reads its colours only (layouts, carousels and artwork don\'t carry over) and never changes the folder. Check the theme\'s licence before sharing.
This theme doesn\'t define its colours as variables RetroForge can read.
Each preview below is drawn in that theme. Themes change colours, shapes, type and how game lists look.
Retro Game Corps (Russ) writes some of the best guides around. They\'re his own work, so they open on his site. More channels are in the Links tab.
Grab a drink and a snack (as Russ from Retro Game Corps would say), and pick a topic.
New versions come from RetroForge\'s GitHub releases. Android asks you to confirm before anything is installed.
Select to choose your games folder, e.g. an existing \"roms\" folder from another frontend. RetroForge only reads it.

They play fine where they are. Other frontends (RetroArch, ES-DE, RetroBat) want each game in its system\'s folder, though. Select to see them in the ROM Manager: it shows every move first, and History can undo it.
Add your games first. RetroForge then gets the emulators they need by itself.
RetroForge\'s built-in player doesn\'t run these systems yet; see below.
RetroForge downloads these emulators for you in the background.
Install it from Google Play or its website, then open it once and allow it to access files.

RetroArch keeps its emulators (\"cores\") in its own private storage, so only RetroArch can download them: in RetroArch, Main Menu → Online Updater → Core Downloader. Each game\'s page names the core it needs.

Some systems need BIOS files from the original console. RetroForge doesn\'t provide them. If you have your own, select this to choose the folder they\'re in (for example another frontend\'s \"bios\" folder) and RetroForge will check them.
None of the systems in your library need BIOS files.

RetroArch reads BIOS from its own \"system\" folder (normally RetroArch/system on internal storage). Select to copy the files above there under the names the cores expect. Files already there are left alone; nothing is deleted.
You\'ll be asked to choose that folder once. Open RetroArch at least once first so it exists.
You can skip any step and come back later from Settings → Set up RetroForge.
You have every BIOS your games need
Games for these won\'t start in the built-in player until the BIOS is in your BIOS folder:
Three steps from your game folder to playing; most of it happens by itself. You can come back here any time from Settings.

Any game can be shown once per eye: pause it (or swipe in from an edge) and switch on Cardboard VR. The phone turns sideways and the touch buttons hide, so a Bluetooth controller is the way to play. Most games look like a big floating screen; Virtual Boy games are real 3D.
Start every game in Cardboard VR
For a session in the viewer. Any game can still be switched back in its pause menu.
No Virtual Boy games in your library. Add them to a virtualboy folder and they show up here.
Each eye gets its own picture, as on the original console.
Side-by-side and top-and-bottom 3D films play one half per eye; any 2D film can play on a big screen per eye (cinema mode). Your 3D films are below; all films are in Media.
On a Quest, RetroForge runs as a flat Android window: games and films play on a big virtual screen.
Play and watch in a Cardboard-style viewer: put your phone in it sideways.
Gets the latest patch from the hack\'s GitHub releases (%1$s) and opens the patcher with it. Then pick your %2$s ROM.
Read the full description, check which ROM version it needs, and download the patch there. %1$s
Download the catalogue from %1$s? (up to 2 MB)
Showing 30 of %1$s+ matches. Type more to narrow it down.
First time with a core? If RetroArch says the core is missing, open RetroArch → Online Updater → Core Downloader and get \"%1$s\". To come back here, quit the game from RetroArch\'s menu.
Free standalone apps that play %1$s games. RetroForge doesn\'t include them: install the ones you want.

They go to the %1$s folder at the top of %2$s, keeping their folder structure. gamelist.xml entries are pointed at the copy you keep, after saving the original as gamelist.xml.retroforge-backup. Nothing is deleted; delete %3$s yourself once you\'re happy.

Each game is compressed, then read back and checked. Only then do its original files move to the %1$s folder and gamelist.xml / .m3u entries point at the new file. This can take a long time for disc games.
